text:
Marta: heads-up — support ticket #98721: customer reports sustained p99 tail increase for hosted API in us-west starting ~09:10 UTC. They measured ~1.6s p99 (previously ~0.3s) and attached a few X-Request-IDs: r-44e6, r-44e9, r-4500.
Kevin: I see the alert firing in latency-sigmon. Snapshot: https://grafana.redwood.company/d/abcd123/latency-overview?from=1721002000000&to=1721004000000
Ana: Quick question — which signal does our dashboard p99 show? rollup gauge or computed histogram_quantile? The semantics differ.
Luis: The problematic panel is wired to `redwood.api.request_duration_p99_rollup{env="prod",region="us-west"}`. That's our 1m rollup gauge emitted by the lightweight collector. The raw histogram lives in `request_duration_bucket`.
Marta: Customer traces they've provided show many sub-100ms requests and a few outliers around 1s. That pattern can blow up a small-sample rollup p99 but the histogram-based quantile over many requests would be lower.
Kevin: I ran two queries to compare:

```
# rollup gauge (cheap)
redwood.api.request_duration_p99_rollup{region="us-west"}

# histogram-based (accurate-ish, heavier)
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_duration_bucket[5m])) by (le))
```

Results at ~09:15: rollup ≈ 1.6s, hist_quantile ≈ 0.45s. They diverge.
Ana: That explains the support escalation. Our alerts are tied to the rollup to save query cost, which means alerting on rollup can be noisy for taily workloads.
oncall-bot: @Marta @Kevin Incident INC-3421 created — severity: p2 — assigned: eng-platform
Support Agent: Customer wants an explanation and mitigation ASAP; they're SLA-sensitive and asked for a post-mortem. They provided the X-Request-IDs above.
Luis: I inspected node logs and kube events. Around 09:05 node `gpu-12` saw OOM churn — kubelet restarted several pods. Some in-flight requests were retried and landed on other nodes. Retry headers show up in several traces.
Marta: Do retries explain part of the tail? If a request is retried and both attempts are counted separately in metrics, that could skew p99.
Kevin: I tried reproducing a sample with the customer's X-Request-ID header:

```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -H "X-Request-ID: r-44e6" "https://api.redwood.dev/v1/generate" -d '{"input":"test"}'

# sample response headers
server-timing: app;dur=1203
```

That request showed ~1.2s server-side time.
Ana: So we have two compounding contributors: (1) a real, limited infra jitter on a subset of nodes producing real tail latencies; (2) a rollup gauge that overstates p99 in presence of low-volume outliers because it samples collector maxima rather than weighting by volume.
Luis: Agreed. Rollup sampler behavior: picks from a few scrape sources and ends up amplifying low-volume high-latency samples.
Kevin: Immediate mitigation proposal (short window):
- Temporarily change alert expression for us-west to histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_duration_bucket[5m])) by (le)) — more accurate.
- Create an Alertmanager override to silence the rollup-based alert for 30m.
- Cordon + drain node `gpu-12` to remove the churn source.
- Ask support to collect ~10 failing request IDs and offer a one-time credit if SLA impacted.

Marta: Which of these can be executed within 15 minutes?
Luis: I can cordon and start draining `gpu-12` now (need SRE approval for heavy pods). Commands:

```
kubectl cordon node/gpu-12 && kubectl drain node/gpu-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data
```

Expect ~3-6 minutes for evictions depending on pod grace periods.
Ana: I will open a short-lived PR to alerting-rules switching region=us-west to histogram_quantile. CI + deploy should be ~10m. I'll also add an annotation to the dashboard describing the two signals.
Kevin: I'll create a one-off Alertmanager override entry and silence the rollup alert for 30 minutes: `override-INC-3421`.
oncall-bot: @Ana Alert override created: override-INC-3421 — expires in 30m
Support Agent: Please confirm the wording before we reply to the customer. They asked: is this a dashboard bug or an actual regression?
Marta: Draft reply to customer:

"Thanks for the report. We investigated and found two contributors: (1) a transient node-level issue that caused some requests to have increased server-side latency, and (2) a difference in how our dashboard computes p99 — the rollup gauge can amplify rare outliers. We have evacuated the affected node and temporarily switched alerting to histogram-based p99 while we validate. We'll follow up with a short post-mortem and remediation plan."

Does that sound right? :thumbsup?
Kevin: Looks good. Ask them for any additional X-Request-IDs if they have them and whether they saw retries client-side.
Luis: Post-incident action items (to attach to INC-3421):
- Add sample_count and sample_ts metrics to rollup exporter so we can audit weighting.
- Evaluate moving rollup aggregator to a volume-weighted algorithm or expose both signals together.
- Improve retry logic so user-visible requests aren't retried silently in ways that skew observability or billing.
- Add a canary/autofallback to route traffic away from nodes showing rising queue_depth or >X% OOM restarts.

Ana: Observability follow-ups:
- Add a dashboard row that shows `rollup_p99` vs `hist_p99` side-by-side with a tooltip on semantic differences.
- Add a PromQL helper panel for SREs to compare queries used by alarms vs raw histograms.
- Link to current investigation panel: https://grafana.redwood.company/d/abcd123/latency-us-west?var-region=us-west

Marta: Support will send the drafted message after we confirm the node drain succeeded. Also recommend offering a goodwill credit if SLA impacted.
Support Agent: Sending message to customer now; will forward any more request IDs we get.
Kevin: Follow-ups to track:
- Does divergence persist after `gpu-12` evacuation? If yes, escalate to EPIC.
- Check billing metrics: are retries double-counting usage toward customer quota?

Ana: I'll open ENG-EPIC-5267 "rollup p99 parity & weighting" and attach the investigation notes and PromQL snippets.
Luis: Node drain finished; pods recreated on other nodes. Monitoring looks better but continuing to observe collector-level p99s.
oncall-bot: INC-3421 status update: mitigation-in-progress — next update in 30m — assigned: eng-platform
Marta: Thanks everyone. Please paste any correlated trace IDs into the incident ticket and we'll reconvene in 30 minutes to decide on further remediation (rollback or longer infra change).
